Story A:

Grass is food. I eat grass and I not die.

Farmer is friend. I not kill farmer and farmer take me to new grass. I eat new grass and I not die.

Sometimes farmer take me to milk square and invisible calves feed, sometimes farmer take me to bed square and visible calves feed.

When visible calves grow they go away. Invisible calves never grow, always hungry.

Old cows sometimes go away. Maybe someday I go away too. I wonder what away is like. Maybe away have better grass.

Story B:

"Mind you put on your best behavior when we meet the king," Master Hniu said from my side. "Any disrespect like that time with the Burned God, and we might both be skewered on a spit."

I snorted in reply. It was enough to set him chuckling. If not for the fact that my shoulders towered over most grown men, and my hide able to repel even the most well-crafted of spears, I still had my magic to use in the event of ... unruly behavior from men.

Master Hniu and the All-cow, they called us. Far and wide we had traveled, welcome in every village, venerated in every town. This King Pawrut was a stranger to us, an Islander, yet even our tales had reached his court and earned us an invitation to visit.

Master Hniu knuckled his back, leaning more heavily against his staff with every step. I winced and nudged his cheek in apology, but he brushed me away. It was my fault, after all. I hadn't enjoyed the boat ride, so I'd willed into existence a strong, wooden bridge from the mainland. He'd been looking forward to a restful journey over two days; instead, we'd walked for close to a week.

As always, he never complained. The King had called, and so we came.

As we neared the top of Kingmount, a small hill in the center of this city of mud-brick houses upon which his palace sat, I noticed the presence of more and more people who appeared to be awaiting our presence. They wore dark-colored clothes that smelled like sea-grass, holding out colorful shells to us in their cupped palms as we passed.

Master Hniu didn't take any, but bowed to some and spoke quietly to others. To me, he whispered, "These people are very poor. Look at their bare feet; their hair is dirty, and many are starved."

Despite decades of being with him, hearing his platitudes, I'd never quite understood what wealth or poverty meant in human terms. So what if their feet were bare? My hooves had never seen the insides of a shoe, ever! Even Master Hniu shunned footwear of any sort. As for starvation, there was grass aplenty everywhere. If they ate the grass they collected instead of weaving them into clothing, they would have plenty.

Nonetheless, I knew what Master Hniu was going to suggest. So I concentrated, and suddenly a mountain of loaves appeared upon an empty patch of stone by the side of the congregation. There was the briefest pause of shock among the people, and then a roar from dozens of throats as excitement took hold. They rushed to the pile, shoving each other aside, looking almost like a stampede of my wilder fellows fleeing the lion.

Master Hniu sighed unhappily. "I've told you, no piles! One loaf in each hand."

I shrugged and followed him and a pair of guards through the palace doors. The building was carved into the top part of the hill itself, a conical mound decorated on the outside with epics depicting royalty or some such. I feigned interest when the guards tried to explain some of them, and licked at a patch of sweetweed that grew through a crack in the stone.

At last, we were ushered into the king's chambers, one filled with shadows cast by paltry candles. Master Hniu rubbed his hands together, his breath misting in front of him.

We were told to halt in front of the throne, and Master Hniu promptly bowed. I studied King Pawrut. He was young, probably half as old as Master Hniu. He wore clothing made of silk and cotton, and earth metals decorated him instead of shellfish. His dark eyes roved between us, calculative.

"So, you're the legendary duo I've been hearing so much about," he said.

"Yes, your Majesty," Master Hniu said. "Thank you for—"

King Pawrut waved a hand to silence Master Hniu. "Cow. You understand what I say, yes?"

I mooed gently in affirmation.

He considered it for a moment before nodding to himself. "Good, good. My, look at you. Guards, a big one, don't you agree? Well, it's not the size I care about, I'm not going to eat you."

He laughed, and was echoed by his retinue. Master Hniu touched me gently, to reassure me. Not that I needed it.

"So, let's get down to it, shall we? I want gold, a fleet of warships and a beautiful princess. Simple enough. That's what you do, isn't it? You grant wishes."

"Pardon, your Majesty, but—"

The king brought his palm down on the throne. "I wasn't talking to you, peasant. I'm talking to your cow, strange as it may be for you to grasp. Now, where were we?"

"I will not be spoken to like that."

A hush fell upon the court. The king's eyes bulged as he stared at Master Hniu, who took a step forward.

"This cow is not property; she is a friend who trusts me to speak for her. So I tell you this, King Pawrut. You have offered us no courtesy from the moment we walked in here. Do you know what I was doing two weeks ago? Brokering peace between two warring nations. All-Cow ended a sixty-year famine in the Withered Steppes before that. We are not your subjects to command and bully. Mind you get that into your crowned skull."

King Pawrut looked as though he'd been slapped, and more than a few people gasped.

Suddenly, he smiled and said, "It was only a test, honored guests. Food and drink will be brought for you. Please rest, you must be so tired after your miraculous journey over the sea to my kingdom. We shall talk about your power later."

Master Hniu scowled. "Beg pardon, your Majesty, but you seem to be missing the point. There will be no power, no wishes. All-Cow does as All-Cow wishes. Neither you nor I can force her."

The king's expression instantly turned ugly. "Is that so?" he said softly. "I've waited on this cold stone for two weeks, waiting for you ungrateful scoundrels to show up. And then you stroll in at your leisure, and tell me you won't even grant me a few basic things?"

Master Hniu opened his mouth to argue, but the king shouted, "Don't you dare accuse me of anything, old man! You don't know what it's like, being raided by pirates for three seasons in a year! Being poor, being cut off from trade!"

"And the princess?" Master Hniu interjected.

"No royal blood has visited us in years, and no king will promise his daughter to me. My lineage is all but doomed!"

I silently thought about the numerous females outside, who seemed to be perfectly suited for mating. Then again, I'd never mated in my life either; somehow, when you could command rain and raise mountains, bulls seemed extremely ... trivial.

"Very well. The first two we can, but All-Cow cannot create humans out of thin air. Nor can she bend a person's will."

The king clenched a fist. "Worthless. What use are either of you to me, then? In my kingdom, we have a law against charlatans."

Just like that, we were surrounded by a ring of spear-wielding guards. Their leather armor smelled of kin, tempting me to lower my horns. Master Hniu must have sensed my discomfort, for he said, "Make no move, All-Cow. Peace must be maintained, above—augh!"

A trio of guards plunged their spears. The rest struck me, but the blows were harmless. The king hopped up and down on his dais, jeering and calling us liars.

Red filled my vision; not of liquid life, but my friend sinking to the ground, his hand resting against my side. His eyes were wide with pain, and blood bubbled from his lips.

I bellowed in rage and summoned my will. Immediately, the guards crumpled to the ground as piles of thick grass. The king shrieked in fear, and then he too lay inert and fragrant on his throne, a fuzzy mound of green.

I bared my teeth, preparing to consume the murderers, but Master Hniu's voice found me one last time. "Peace, friend."

And then the light went out from his eyes. I threw my head back and mooed in anguish. The ground trembled and split beneath my hooves; the throne shattered into dust, the physical manifestation of my broken heart.

Finally, as the sound of my cries died away and a crowd of fearful, whispering people had gathered at the entrance to the room, I lowered my head to touch Master Hniu's. Slowly, his body and clothes melted, turning into a carpet of gentle, leafy grass; the kind he loved to sit on. Flowers sprouted and bloomed, consuming his head, leaving his final, smile for last.

Then I lay down upon my friend, and remembered the happiest life a cow could have had.

***

*Thanks for reading, hope you enjoyed it. Check out my [sub](http://reddit.com/r/nonsenselocker) for more stories!*

transcript.message:
Both stories present unique narratives, but they differ significantly in their execution and overall impact.

**Story A** creates a simple, straightforward narrative from the perspective of a cow, effectively conveying its understanding of life and relationships with the farmer. The prose is deliberately simplistic, reflecting the character's limited cognitive ability. The repetition of phrases enhances the storytelling, highlighting the cow's thoughts and observations. However, while it charmingly captures the essence of life from an animal's point of view, the emotional impact feels muted due to the lack of deeper conflict and emotional exploration.

**Story B**, on the other hand, showcases a much richer tapestry of creativity through complex world-building and character dynamics. The cow, endowed with magical abilities, and its relationship with Master Hniu, builds a powerful narrative arc that explores themes of friendship, respect, and the heart-wrenching ramifications of violence. The dialogue is sharp and engaging, enhancing narrative coherence as it progresses toward a poignant climax. This story also delivers a strong emotional impact, especially with the tragic moment of loss, which resonates deeply with readers.

In terms of creativity, narrative coherence, emotional impact, and writing quality, **Story B** surpasses **Story A** with its intricate characters and layered storytelling.

Final choice: Story B

Both stories present unique perspectives and styles, but let’s evaluate them according to the criteria provided.

### Creativity
**Story A** offers a straightforward narrative from the perspective of a cow, exploring simple but poignant themes of existence, companionship, and the uncertainty of the future. Its simplicity adds to its charm, with a distinctive voice that brings forth its unique take on life from an animal's perspective.

**Story B**, on the other hand, presents a whimsical and rich fantasy world populated by magical elements, social commentary on wealth and poverty, and character dynamics between a wise old man and a sentient cow. The interplay between human characters and the cow's perception of what it means to be "poor" versus "wealthy" is inventive and layered.

### Narrative Coherence
**Story A** maintains a clear and coherent narrative thread, focusing on the cow's mundane life without deviating from its central theme. The progression of thoughts is logical and easily followed.

**Story B** showcases a more complex narrative involving various characters and themes. While it is generally well-structured, there are moments where the depth of the world-building and dialogue may overwhelm the reader. However, the overarching story remains coherent as it intertwines themes of conflict, friendship, and transformation.

### Emotional Impact
**Story A** provides subtle emotional depth, invoking feelings of nostalgia and curiosity about life and loss. The cow's reflections on companionship and the uncertainty of its own fate resonate with readers on a fundamental level.

**Story B** elicits a stronger emotional response due to its dramatic conflict and poignant ending. The loss of Master Hniu, the cow's best friend, is heart-wrenching and adds layers of suffering and love. The transformation of Master Hniu into grass serves as a powerful metaphor for grief and memory, enhancing the emotional weight of the story.

### Writing Quality
**Story A** uses simple language fitting its narrator, which adds an authentic touch to a cow's voice. However, it may be perceived as less polished than the complex prose of the second story.

**Story B** employs rich imagery, varied sentence structure, and a well-developed voice for its characters. The dialogue is engaging and often witty, lending itself to both fantasy and realism. The overall writing quality is higher due to its complexity and engagement with multiple themes.

### Conclusion
While both stories have their merits, **Story B** excels in creative depth and emotional resonance. It combines fantasy with strong character dynamics and a dramatic conclusion that leaves a lasting impression. 

Final choice: Story B

When evaluating both stories, we can see distinctions in creativity, narrative coherence, emotional impact, and writing quality.

**Creativity**: 
Story B showcases a highly imaginative world where a cow possesses magical powers alongside a human companion. The dialogue and dynamics between the characters provide a rich landscape of fantasy grounded in a relatable emotional journey. Story A, however, presents a more minimalist and simplistic narrative from the perspective of a cow, which, while interesting, lacks the breadth and complexity of Story B.

**Narrative Coherence**:
Story B's plot unfolds with a clear structure, following a journey with a set goal (meeting the king) that results in a powerful climax and resolution. It weaves together the elements of storytelling adeptly, leading to a coherent and engaging narrative with tension and character development. In contrast, Story A presents a more fragmented thought process from the cow's perspective that, while coherent as a stream of consciousness, feels less complete in terms of narrative arc and depth.

**Emotional Impact**:
Story B excels in emotional resonance, particularly in the final moments where the cow experiences profound grief and transformation. The relationship between the cow and Master Hniu adds layers of poignancy, evoking empathy and sadness. Story A, while it effectively conveys existential thoughts and a cow’s simple perspective on life and death, ultimately does not have the same depth of emotional engagement or connection to the reader.

**Writing Quality**:
Both stories have a strong voice, but Story B employs more sophisticated descriptive language, varied sentence structures, and character dialogue that enriches the reading experience. Story A, though stylistically unique in capturing the cow’s limited viewpoint, uses repetition and simplicity which might not resonate as strongly with all readers.

In conclusion, while both stories provide valuable insights from their respective viewpoints, Story B clearly stands out in terms of creativity, coherence, emotional impact, and overall writing quality. It delivers a memorable experience that combines fantasy, character depth, and profound emotional stakes.

Final choice: Story B

Upon reviewing both narratives, here are the evaluations based on the criteria provided:

**Creativity:**
- **Story A** approaches its theme from a unique perspective—that of a cow reflecting on its experiences with a farmer and the concept of "away." This limited viewpoint offers a fresh take on the life of farm animals, showcasing simplicity and innocence.
- **Story B** features an imaginative scenario involving a magical cow and its human companion traveling to meet a king. The plot integrates elements of magic, humor, and social commentary, enhancing the creativity present in the narrative.

**Narrative Coherence:**
- **Story A** has a straightforward narrative that is coherent and easy to follow, focusing on a singular perspective with clear expressions of thought. The simplicity serves the story's themes well, although the limited outside context can feel sparse.
- **Story B** has a complex plot involving multiple characters, dialogue, and dramatic tension. While it provides a rich narrative experience, at times, its transitions may feel densely packed, making the intricate plot a bit harder to grasp without careful reading.

**Emotional Impact:**
- **Story A**, while lacking in complexity, evokes emotions through its simplicity and the underlying thoughts of the cow about life, freedom, and loss. There is a subtly poignant reflection on existence and the desire for better circumstances.
- **Story B** possesses substantial emotional impact, particularly in the climax where the bond between the cow and Master Hniu is showcased. The grief and tragedy of losing a beloved friend create a strong emotional resonance, making the reader feel the depth of loss alongside the protagonist.

**Writing Quality:**
- **Story A** is written in minimalist prose that matches the character's perspective but may be viewed by some as lacking depth or literary sophistication.
- **Story B** is more layered in its writing style, presenting a blend of humor, drama, and clear characterization, along with vivid descriptions that enhance the storytelling.

In summary, while both stories have their merits, Story B exhibits greater creativity, emotional depth, and writing quality. The complexity of its narrative, combined with the rich backdrop and character development, gives it a definitive edge.

Final choice: Story B
